dimensions.assessment: Affects tax professionals, software providers, financial institutions, state tax agencies, and individual or corporate taxpayers using electronic filing.
dimensions.evidence: An EFIN may not be used to electronically file any return or other document unless the Secretary has confirmed that such EFIN has been validated

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new operational and technological compliance requirements on software systems and tax preparers without altering tax liability rules.
dimensions.evidence: provide a real-time system for the validation of EFINs

dimensions.assessment: Requires the IRS to develop and maintain a real-time validation program and data disclosure framework, though exact implementation costs are not stated.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall develop a program for the validation of EFINs.

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new mandatory verification regime, amends Internal Revenue Code disclosure provisions (Section 6103), and mandates integration into electronic filing software.
dimensions.evidence: Section 6103(k) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent ongoing validation requirements for future tax filing years starting after a two-year implementation delay.
dimensions.evidence: this section shall apply to returns and other documents filed with respect to taxable years beginning after the date that is 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific federal appropriations or funding figures needed to build and operate the real-time validation system.
The specific criteria the Secretary will use to approve 'specified validators'.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 10334 requires real-time validation of electronic filing identification numbers (EFINs) by the IRS or specified validators before tax returns can be filed electronically.
